clue.text: Quick easy victory, something precious about it

indicators.note: the precious-metal symbol goes round the easy win, so 'about it' signals a container

parts.note: PT is the chemical symbol for platinum, a precious metal
a romp is an easy, one-sided win

explanation.surface: A sports report: a fast, easy win with some precious trophy wrapped around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a prompt reply is a speedy, immediate one.

clue.text: Secure banking payment, crude stuff

indicators.note: to bank something is to hold it inside, so the fastener encloses the payment

parts.note: to pin something is to secure it
a giro is a British bank transfer or benefit payment

explanation.surface: Locking away a bank payment, described as crude business.
explanation.walkthrough: A GIRO is a British payment by bank transfer, once the usual way state benefits were paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig iron is the crude metal straight from the blast furnace, before refining.

clue.text: Start acting?

definitions.meaning: an actor at work is on the film set, read as two words

explanation.surface: A director's question: start acting?
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the onset of something is its start; split in two, actors performing are on set.

clue.text: Slovakia and Jamaica (via Romania) both have breakfast

definitions.text: Slovakia and Jamaica (via Romania) both have breakfast

parts.words: Slovakia and Jamaica (via Romania) both have breakfast
parts.note: slOVAkia holds OVA, Latin ..., and jamaiCA VIA Romania holds CAVIAR, fish ...: each has ... stolen inside it

explanation.surface: Two nations, one routed through Romania, sharing the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' means the eggs are snatched inside the place names: OVA in Slovakia and CAVIAR across 'Jamaica via Romania'. Eggs taken from inside are eggs illegally taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs cooked by simmering out of the shell are a standard breakfast dish, and to poach also means to take illicitly.

clue.text: Creative mind taking an age to orbit Pluto

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
the age circles the god of the underworld, so it goes around him

parts.note: an eon is an immensely long age
Dis is the Roman name for Pluto, god of the underworld

explanation.surface: An inventive thinker taking aeons to circle the dwarf planet Pluto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluto' looks astronomical but is the underworld god, DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison, prolific inventor of the light bulb and phonograph, is a famous creative mind.

clue.text: Bored, it's suggested, with one in ruin

indicators.note: 'bored' suggests 'fed up', and in a down clue 'up' means the word is written upwards

parts.note: fed up means bored
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone bored, with a single player involved in ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal indicator is implied: Bored = 'fed up', and FED read up gives DEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to deface a wall or monument is to spoil or ruin it.

clue.text: Run off and drained like 9?

parts.note: scram means go away quickly
bled means drained of blood or funds

explanation.surface: Someone fled and was exhausted, a bit like eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is EGGS, so the definition is a style of cooked eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs beaten and stirred in the pan are a classic way to cook them.

clue.text: News about diversion of route — no charge for it

indicators.note: the news letters go around the rearranged road word

parts.note: N is new; read as a plural, news gives two of them

indicators.note: a diversion sends traffic a different way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traffic bulletin about a road diversion, saying no charge is made for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion of' rearranges the road word to EUTRO. Plural 'News' as two Ns is a liberty the solver must accept.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutron is the subatomic particle carrying no electric charge, a clever spin on a free service.

clue.text: Smart as a cyanide-laced salad?

definitions.meaning: a poisoned salad has had a deadly dressing put on it

explanation.surface: A poisoner's dinner party: smart, like a salad laced with cyanide.
explanation.walkthrough: Salad dressing laced with poison makes a salad dressed to murder.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone dressed glamorously to impress is said to be dressed in this way.

clue.text: See 3
Golden fur is a euro — that's fake?

indicators.note: a fake is a counterfeit, so the letters are made into something different

explanation.surface: Gold-coloured fur and a euro coin are both counterfeit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's fake' rearranges FURISAEURO.
explanation.definitionFit: Auriferous means gold-bearing, from Latin aurum; 'golden' in the sense of containing gold.

clue.text: Bum soaked, last of water going in with both taps

indicators.note: the final letter of the water goes inside the damp word

parts.note: wet means soaked

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word water is used

parts.note: taps are marked C and H, cold and hot

explanation.surface: A down-and-out, soaked through, with water running from both taps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' picks R from water; 'going in' puts it inside WET.
explanation.definitionFit: A bum is a vagrant or worthless person, a miserable wretch.

clue.text: Growth of many branches as US retailer backs Scandinavian currency

indicators.note: goes backwards, so the store's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Macy's is the New York department store chain
the ore is a small coin of Sweden, Norway and Denmark

explanation.surface: A big business story: an American chain expands, backing a Nordic currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' reverses MACYS to SYCAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree is a growth with many branches; the sycamore is a large spreading example.

clue.text: Threw good 9s like this? Some initially getting caught

indicators.note: the first letter is trapped inside the description of the eggs

parts.note: good eggs are not rotten, that is not addled

indicators.note: just the first letter of the word some

explanation.surface: A rider's mount threw off perfectly good eggs, some getting caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives S; 'getting caught' puts it inside UNADDLED. Addled eggs are rotten, so good ones are un-addled. Paul probably meant 'good 9' not '9s'.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that unseats its rider has thrown them out of the saddle.

clue.text: A law together with sovereign pontiff

parts.note: lex is Latin for law
and joins things together
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A legal decree combined with royal authority from the Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight popes took this name, so a pontiff could be one, an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Pastry dish for lunch about noon, originally

indicators.note: the original letters are the beginnings of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Planning a tart to serve for lunch, around twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the opening letters of four words.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a filling, a pastry dish.

clue.text: Where tools may be dropped

definitions.meaning: a garden hut where tools are stored
cast off, as in skin or leaves

explanation.surface: Where you might put your tools down.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden hut stores tools; and a snake that dropped its skin is said to have cast it off.

clue.text: Bear most upset over a chimp, no little monkey

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are disordered
the small creature is removed from the ape

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a little monkey

explanation.surface: A zoo-keeper's lament: grumpy over a chimp that is no little monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes STOM from MOST; 'no' removes IMP from CHIMP, leaving CH.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate it, to bear it.

clue.text: Hearing nothing, notes fade badly

indicators.note: played badly, the letters come out wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A deaf listener hears nothing as the musical notes fade out badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges NOTESFADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone totally deaf hears no sound at all.

clue.text: Nothing very exciting nearby, both heading northward from Reno, say?

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: nada is Spanish for nothing

indicators.note: the heads, or first letters, of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A traveller heading north from Reno finds nothing exciting nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both heading' takes E and N; 'northward' reverses NADAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Reno is a city in Nevada, so someone from there is a native of that state, hence the 'say?'.

clue.text: Some boxing leading to riot

indicators.note: boxing means putting into a box, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: any means some
arch means chief or leading, as in archenemy

explanation.surface: A bit of boxing escalates into a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport; it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: riot, used loosely of total disorder and lawlessness.

clue.text: Little time in short tragedy, it's noted

indicators.note: the brief time sits inside the cut-down tragedy title
short means missing its last letter

parts.note: Faust is Goethe's tragedy
a mo is a moment, a little time

explanation.surface: A moment in a brief tragedy that is widely remarked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the final T; Faust is Goethe's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a noted person is well known, celebrated.

clue.text: Weapon — but isn't Jerry a pacifist?

definitions.meaning: a Native American axe used as a weapon
in the cartoon the cat chasing Jerry mouse would be the aggressive one, the warmonger, if Jerry is the dove

explanation.surface: A weapon, but surely the mouse in the cartoon is peace-loving?
explanation.walkthrough: In Tom and Jerry, if Jerry is a pacifist, then Tom is a hawk, read as TOM A HAWK.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomahawk is a light axe used as a weapon by Native Americans.

clue.text: Pure way to cut meat

indicators.note: the road abbreviation cuts into the meat, sitting inside it

parts.note: veal is calf meat
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A clean way to slice meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Vestal virgins were chaste priestesses of Rome, so the adjective means chaste and pure.

clue.text: Bind bits up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: parts are bits

explanation.surface: Tie the pieces together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses PARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to strap something is to fasten or bind it with a belt.

clue.text: Cold as 9?

definitions.meaning: the 9 entry is EGGS, so a way of cooking them firm in the shell

explanation.surface: Cold, like eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough, cynical detective is hard-boiled; and eggs boiled firm are the cooking sense.

clue.text: Deep fried successor for Nietzsche?

definitions.meaning: deep as in a full, intense colour or sound
the philosopher's first name begins Fried-, and what follows those letters is the rest

explanation.surface: Deep-fried food fit for the German philosopher Nietzsche.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep fried' looks like a phrase; split it. Friedrich Nietzsche's first name continues after 'Fried'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a rich, deep voice or colour is full and intense.

clue.text: Not entirely leporine animal, an equine badger!

indicators.note: not all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: leporine means relating to hares
an ass is a donkey, a member of the horse family

explanation.surface: Half a hare and a donkey, an equine badger: a strange menagerie!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops the last letter of HARE. 'badger' looks like the animal but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to badger someone is to pester them persistently.

clue.text: Smart putting waste collector behind skip for a start

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first
just the starting letter of the word skip

parts.note: a nappy collects a baby's waste

explanation.surface: Clever thinking: put the waste collector behind the skip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a start' takes S from skip; 'behind' puts NAPPY after it. A skip is a British builder's waste container, and a nappy is a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a snappy dresser is smart, stylish.
